match.reason: None of the bank points teaches redeploying existing resources within a business to where they add more value; the closest, bus-business-resources, only defines resource types and how to weigh them when choosing what to use, and the economics points cover PPFs and LRAS shifts rather than business reallocation.

draft.title: Redeployment of resources
card: Redeployment means moving a resource from one use to another inside the same business. The aim is to put it where it adds more value.
Natural
resources taken from the earth, such as land, timber or water. A farm might shift land from a falling crop to a more profitable one.
Labour
the skills and effort of staff. A retailer might move staff from a shrinking store to its growing online team.
Capital
made items used to produce, such as machines, vehicles and buildings. A bakery might move an oven from a quiet shop to a busy one.
draft.remember: Redeployment keeps resources in the business but moves them to where they add more value.

a.q: A bank closes a quiet branch and moves its tellers to its busy online help team. What is this an example of?
opts: Redeployment of labour resources
Redeployment of capital resources
Redeployment of natural resources
Cutting costs by reducing staff numbers
a.why: Staff are labour, and they stay with the bank but do a new job where more work is needed. Cost cutting is tempting, but nobody has left the business, so this is redeployment.
a.clue: Who is being moved, people or equipment?

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Geelong. Her second shop is quiet, so she moves its spare oven to her busy main shop to lift output. What has she done?
opts: Redeployed a capital resource to a higher value use
Redeployed a labour resource to a higher value use
Sold a capital resource to raise cash for the business
Bought a new capital resource to expand the business
b.why: An oven is a made item used to produce, so it is capital. It stays inside the business and moves to where it adds more value. Selling or buying would bring money or equipment in or out, but nothing leaves or enters here.
b.clue: Is the oven bought, sold or just moved?

b.best: Redeployed a capital resource to a higher value use

problems.detail: The question nearly repeats the card's own example, a bakery moving an oven from a quiet shop to a busy one. It tests recall of the card rather than applying the idea to a new case, which is too easy for Year 12.
The clue 'Is the oven bought, sold or just moved?' rules out two options and points straight to 'moved', leaving only the labour and capital choice.
